photos.c:
Some interesting styles in baton changing at the 100 x 1 mile relay.
Top left. Kevin Clarke (83) demonstrates the cross leg shuffle as he takes the baton from new member L.Lyons.
Top right. M.Harrison (13) demonstrates the walkers change as he hands over to P.Moysey.
Bottom left. Steve Webb (69) milkman to the last gives Pat Lyttle no change.
Centre. Ian Morton (75) provides a fine example of the jumping high level pass with Graham Allerton intercepting.
Bottom right. Colin Pearson (84) uses the jumping low level pass to send Tony Fairclough on his way.
The one man club team. Pat Lyttle who defeated 2 clubs single handed in a Rossenheim League match.
The one man club team. Pat Lyttle who defeated 2 clubs single handed in a Rossenheim League match.

TEAM SPIRIT

Tremendous team spirit has been a key feature off all the British League fixtures this year. When Pat Lyttle put in his best performance to date in winning the 'B' string 100m and 200m at the Warley meeting the first to congratulate him was jumps Captain Derrick Williams. This picture records Derricks only moment of inactivity as he amassed 30 points from; High Jump, Long Jump, Triple Jump, 100m and 400m Relay Squads.
Pat Lyttle heads the field at the first takeover in the British League Match 3 which we won so convincingly at Windsor.

PHOTOS FROM THE CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS

Joe Minetti (33) completes a sprint double by winning the 200m from Stuart Paton who clocked a nippy 22.9 - not bad for a middle distance man! Others in shot , left to right, are Mike Scott, Andy Paton, Phil Smith and Pat Lyttle

Gordon Biscoe appears to be looking at the watch in disbelief but it was a comfortable 58 at the bell for Richard O'Hara who ran out an easy winner. Alan Painter, a youngster of 39, was the only other runner inside 2 minutes. Pat Lyttle is still in touch at this point but his legs are about to part company with the rest of his body any second!
